sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:23240
Court No. - 28

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 11926 of 2023
Applicant :- Nandu Alias Atul Kumar Dwivedi

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Govt. Civil Sectt. Lko And 3 Othe
Counsel for Applicant :- Mohd.Mateen,Vikas Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Brij Raj Singh,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of applicant is taken on record.
2. Heard Shri Mohd. Mateen, learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Avishesh Kumar Singh, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.
Though notice upon complainant has been served sufficiently, no one has appeared.

3. The present bail application has been filed by the applicant with a prayer to enlarge him on bail in Case Crime No.158 of 2023, under Sections-363, 366, 376 I.P.C.,& Section 3/4 POCSO Act and Section 3 (2) (v) SC/ST Act, P.S.-Kotwali Dehat, District Balrampur.
4. This is the second bail application.
The first bail application was dismissed as not pressed on 20.09.2023.
Thereafter, this Court granted interim bail to the applicant on 02.11.2023 with the condition that the applicant will marry the prosecutrix within three months.
5. In compliance of the order dated 02.11.2023, the marriage certificate has been annexed along with supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.
Learned counsel has submitted that the applicant and the prosecutrix are living as husband and wife.

It has been further submitted that the Nandu Alias Atul Kumar Dwivedi vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101113485/
1 statement of the prosecutrix under Section 164 Cr.P.C. indicates that physical relation was established out of her free will and she was in love with the applicant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The statement also indicates that the prosecutrix was a consenting party.
The applicant has no criminal history as such he is entitled to be released on bail.
6. Learned AGA has opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the aforesaid fact that the marriage of the applicant has been performed with the prosecutrix.

7. Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and after hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the fact that marriage between applicant and prosecutrix has been performed; argument that both are living as husband and wife; argument that the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. of the prosecutrix indicates that she was a consenting party and physical relation was established out of free will, therefore, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

8. Let the applicant, Nandu @ Atul Kumar Dwivedi be released on bail in the above case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

9. It is made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The Trial Court shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions on the Nandu Alias Atul Kumar Dwivedi vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...
